incident-bot: [INCIDENT CREATED] INC-2026-042 - High KV heap growth on rope-serving nodes (NTK + longctx traffic). Pager fired at 19:17 UTC. Potential customer impact: generation latency spikes, 5% error rate increase.

alex_k: I’m on it. seeing a cluster of nodes in us-west-2 with sustained RSS growth, GC pressure, and eviction thrashing. heatmap: https://rdwd/heat/ntk-1936 :eyes:

maria_s: can you paste the top offending logs? suspected continuous-batch hold-up from longctx + sliding-window prefetch.

alex_k: logs (tail):
```
2026-03-12T19:15:03Z rope[serve]: kv_get miss=0.84 hit=0.16 bucket=ntk-window
2026-03-12T19:15:04Z rope[serve]: batch_enqueue tokens=13472 batch_sz=128 latency_ms=4200
2026-03-12T19:15:05Z rope[serve]: kv_prefetch queued=97 inflight=24
2026-03-12T19:15:06Z kernel: oom_score_adj triggered for process rope-worker pid=18223
```

samir: that batch enqueue and high tokens is suspicious. sounds like continuous-batching is accumulating huge prefixes for NTK windows. any recent rollout?

alex_k: we rolled sliding-window v2 yesterday (canary) with more aggressive prefetch + NTK extension for longctx customers. suspect prefetch + longer NTK multiplier is causing many large prefixes to be cached and never evicted.

maria_s: agree. mitigation options: 1) disable prefetch for sliding-window customers, 2) reduce batch max tokens, 3) force KV eviction on hot nodes, 4) temporary routing to smaller-context model variant.

lia_w: I’ll coordinate infra actions. infra-bot, can you trigger emergency cache eviction on the affected hostset and annotate?

infra-bot: running eviction job: `POST /admin/evict?scope=kv&selector=us-west-2:rope-ntk-hot` - job id evict-1936-01. ETA ~30s.

incident-bot: update INC-2026-042 state -> mitigation-in-progress. oncall: alex_k -> handoff planned at 19:45 UTC if unresolved.

alex_k: executing quick hotpatch: lowering `continuous_batch.max_tokens` from `2048` -> `512` and `prefetch.enabled` -> `false` for sliding-window config. Pushing via rollout: `rdctl rollout apply --cfg sliding-window-v2 --set continuous_batch.max_tokens=512 --set prefetch.enabled=false`

maria_s: also reducing NTK multiplier for longctx to 1.2 (was 2.0). snippet we applied: 
```
{ "ntk": { "multiplier": 1.2 },
  "continuous_batch": { "max_tokens": 512, "window_ms": 80 }
}
```

samir: good. watching telemetry: 95th latency dropped from 2.8s -> 650ms on patched nodes within 60s. errors down to baseline. but a few nodes still showing memory churn; infra eviction job completed.

lia_w: rolling hotfix from canary to 50% of NTK nodes now. command: `rdctl rollout promote sliding-window-v2 --pct 50`. I’ve pinned the rest of the fleet to the previous stable model variant for high-QPS customers.

alex_k: note: we also route heavy longctx customers to `model-compact-v1` (shorter KV footprint) for next 2 hours as a safety net. routing rule in place: `policy: prefer-compact-if(kv_hit_rate<0.2 AND request.tokens>2048)`

incident-bot: INC-2026-042 - mitigation: hotpatch applied, eviction completed, partial routing fallback. Customer impact reduced. ETA monitoring window 30m.

maria_s: action items: - postmortem owner: @maria_s - follow-up: add automatic NTK multiplier guard when prefetch enabled - add alert for kv.eviction_rate > 0.1 and batch_enqueue.tokens > 10k.

samir: logs show one customer with repeated longctx sequences causing repeated cache pinning. we should throttle prefetch per-customer. filed: TICKET-3289.

lia_w: prepping handoff notes for tomorrow’s oncall: will include list of affected node ids, command to rollback hotpatch, and the runbook steps we used.

alex_k: marking thread resolved for now. leaving monitoring for 45m. final note: no significant customer data loss, minor latency blips for small subset of long-context customers (~0.3% of revenue traffic) during the 19:12-19:26 UTC window. will escalate to incident review. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INC-2026-042 state -> monitoring. assigned: maria_s. next update due by 20:15 UTC.
